ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the deviation is real, it is not excused, and the fare correction is arithmetic.

DISTANCE. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement, and EV-GPS-00114 records 23.97 km between pickup and dropoff against the 18.0 km booked optimal on EV-TRIP-00114. The excess is 5.97 km, or 33.2%. That passes both establishment (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is ESTABLISHED, but it falls below both materiality gates (over 50% and over 8.0 km), so there is no repeat-deviation uplift and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06. The trip record's rounded 24.0 km is a convenience copy and is not the threshold figure. The trace is unimpaired: 241 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps, no jumps, so POL-RD-07 does not engage.

EXCULPATION. Nothing excuses the excess. EV-CHAT-00114 contains no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 cannot run. There was no pickup or dropoff amendment (POL-RD-05), the vehicle is RYDE_X not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12), and the fare is METERED with no quoted fare (POL-RD-11). The driver's congestion account names no artifact; EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden, while an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight. I have considered the driver's alternative submission that this gap is itself a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. It is not: that trigger requires an exculpatory clause to be invoked against an artifact that is missing, and the driver expressly does not claim POL-RD-03 exoneration and cites no clause or artifact in his own statements, so there is nothing to escalate. A bare traffic excuse does not become an escalation merely because the advisory that would have supported it does not exist; that is what POL-RD-08's discard rule governs. I have checked the other POL-RD-10 triggers: identifiers match, timestamps agree, the trace is not impaired, every charge line has a counterpart, and no refund ceiling is breached. None fires.

RECOMPUTATION (POL-RD-02, METERED).
- charged_total = 58.10
- recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 30.0 optimal min) x 1.6 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 on-route ERP = 41.12 + 0.80 + 2.50 = 44.42
- refund = 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded UP to 13.70

The 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal route and is already comprehended in this figure; under POL-RD-09(1) it is itemised but never added on top. The 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry lies on the optimal route and properly stays with the rider. Both billed gantries sit within 250 m of the trace, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises. The rider keeps the surge he accepted and the platform fee, and pays only the optimal-route distance and time.

OUTCOME. The rider is refunded SGD 13.70; the balance of the charge stands.
